hero.title: Placeholder markers pattern
hero.description: Two markers that keep unconfirmed copy honest: one for wording drafted on the owner's behalf, one for sections only the owner can supply. Both stay visible in production until someone confirms and removes them.

inline.title: Drafted wording (`Placeholder`)
inline.description: Wraps a sentence drafted so the page has something to hold. The dashed outline and badge show it has not been confirmed; hover the badge for the note.

label.title: Localized badge (`label`)
label.description: Pass `label` in the site's language. A Spanish-first site uses `borrador` instead of the English default `draft`.

section.title: Content only the owner can supply (`PlaceholderSection`)
section.description: Renders the section anyway: a visitor-safe “coming soon” line, then the request addressed to the owner. Used for a story, a team, credentials — things that cannot be drafted.

inline.before: The lending library is open on Saturday mornings.
inline.drafted: Borrowers may keep an item for two weeks, and renew it once if nobody is waiting.
inline.note: Drafted from a rough note — the lending terms are not confirmed

label.drafted: Volunteers meet at the north gate before each shift.
label.note: Drafted by us — the meeting point is not confirmed

section.title: How the workshop runs
section.ask: Only you can fill this in: how long does a session run, how many people fit, and what should someone bring? A voice note is fine — we will write it up.
section.why: The section stays on the page so the gap is visible until it is filled.

whenToUse.title: When to use which
items: `Placeholder`: a statement about how the business or organization operates that we wrote and the owner has not confirmed.
`PlaceholderSection`: content only the owner can provide — their story, team, credentials, day-to-day details. Never invent it; mark the gap instead.

Neither: a fact that is simply missing (use “details coming soon” text), interface labels, button text, error-page copy, or anything taken from the owner's own flyers, messages or social posts — that material is already theirs.
Build the section anyway. An omitted section is invisible, and invisible gaps become permanent.

standard.title: Standard
items: Import both from `@/components/patterns/` — never hand-roll a lookalike marker on a site.
`Placeholder` renders inline (a `span`). Put it inside a paragraph or heading; never wrap block elements in it.
Use `note` to say exactly what is unconfirmed, so a reviewer can confirm quickly.
Pass `label` in the site's language (e.g. `borrador`, `Nos falta tu parte`).
Markers are never hidden in production — no build flag, no CSS, no “strip” helper. Shipping the wording unmarked means deleting the wrapper.
Both use shared theme tokens only (`muted`, `muted-foreground`, `background`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `foreground`). A theme's `accent-foreground` must be readable on `accent`.

Wire `npm run drafts` (`tools/list-drafts.mjs`) on any site that uses the markers; it lists every outstanding one, and is how you check nothing is left after removing a wrapper. Remove imports left unused. A documentation page that renders markers on purpose opts out with a `drafts:ignore-file` comment.
